description:
Found 2026-08-12 while ingesting the HTR-10 references.

REPRODUCTION: run an import with the output piped, e.g.

    ./target/release/kovan lit import <pdf> --json-out <a> --markdown-out <b> | head -14

OBSERVED: the summary block prints and LOOKS successful — it even lists json_out and markdown_out paths — but kovan writes those files AFTER emitting the summary. head closes the pipe, kovan takes SIGPIPE, and the files are never written. The visible output gives no hint that anything failed.

EXPECTED: either write the artifacts BEFORE printing the summary that names them, or handle SIGPIPE so a closed stdout does not abort the work. Printing the path of a file that was never created is the part that makes this dangerous rather than merely annoying — the caller has every reason to believe it succeeded.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: the workspace CLAUDE.md mandates kovan for document ingestion, and piping to head is a natural thing to do with a verbose command. An agent or a human could easily believe a document was ingested when nothing was written, and only discover it much later when the archive turns out to be empty.

kovan is a MEMBER CRATE (crates/kovan-cli), so this is a local bug, not a kopitiam upstream issue.

WORKAROUND until fixed: do not pipe kovan lit import; run it bare and check the artifacts exist on disk afterwards.
title: kovan lit import: writes output files AFTER printing its summary, so piping to head silently loses them
